The warmest ocean on Earth is the **Indian Ocean**. 

Because it is landlocked to the north by Asia and lies largely within tropical latitudes, it receives a large amount of solar radiation with limited water circulation to the polar regions. Surface temperatures across much of the tropical Indian Ocean regularly exceed **28°C (82°F)**, and enclosed bodies connected to it, such as the Persian Gulf and Red Sea, can reach even higher temperatures exceeding **32°C to 35°C (90°F–95°F)**.
